title: platform locale table: script-subtag codes (zh-Hant-TW, zh-Hans-CN, zh-Hant-HK) are not read aliases, so a two-script bundle answers them with the first registered zh-* key
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgTqqeHSwZYJmApbDCa

Part of the #29428 family (ruling F of #29349: one platform locale table, read aliases closed). Filing gate: ① a measured gap found by the contract review of PR #30601 (card #30538, comment 6665489168, should-fix S5). ⛔ Not a claim.

**Business reason.** Browsers and operating systems send script-subtag codes (`zh-Hant-TW`, `zh-Hans-CN`, `zh-Hant-HK`). After PR #30601 the server ladder (`resolveLocaleAmong`) maps a requested code through `platformLocaleTagOf` before the base-language step, so `zh-TW` reaches a registered `zh-Hant`. `PLATFORM_LOCALE_READ_ALIASES` (`packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts` :69-75 at `origin/main` `4831d500`) lists `zh`, `zh-CN`, `zh-SG`, `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, `zh-MO` and no script-subtag spelling, so for `zh-Hant-TW` the table step finds nothing and the base-language and first-variant steps answer: over a bundle holding both `zh-CN` and `zh-Hant`, a Traditional-Chinese reader whose client sends `zh-Hant-TW` still gets whichever `zh-*` key was registered first.

## Wanted

- A decision, recorded on this card, on how the table reads script-subtag codes: add the common spellings as read aliases (`zh-Hans-CN`, `zh-Hans-SG` → `zh-Hans`; `zh-Hant-TW`, `zh-Hant-HK`, `zh-Hant-MO` → `zh-Hant`), or map any `zh-Hans-*` / `zh-Hant-*` to its script tag by rule. Ruling F closed the alias list, so widening it may need the maintainer's word; say which.
- Pins for both registration orders against a two-script bundle, on the spec resolver and core's in-memory resolver (the shared case list PR #30601 adds).
- The Console's own picker follows the same table (#30511 / PR #30595).

Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue is:open zh-Hant-TW` → 6 hits; #30538 (the alias step itself), #30603 (skill text), #29428 (the table's tracking card) and three unrelated; none asks for script-subtag aliases. **New.**

Suggested-grade: p3 · a Traditional-Chinese reader on a script-subtag client gets Simplified where a `zh-Hant` bundle exists; the common clients send `zh-TW`.
